title: Serial correlation reduces the relative cost of SST step protection in an AR(1) model
abstract: We extended an independent-noise bound for fits that ignore dated SST offsets. For a common six-date design, optimal linear trend fits retain 13.79% of information in 1982-2022 under independent noise, but 35.18% under stationary monthly AR(1) noise with correlation 0.9. Corresponding 2001-2022 values are 14.76% and 48.11%. At correlation 0.9, ordinary least squares with the same offset constraints has 2.42 and 2.99 times the optimal trend variance. Changing covariance also changes time weights and five-model radiation-to-SST trend ratios. Raw and corrected series still agree by construction. Exact covariance checks, dense solves and stationary-noise simulations support the calculation. High relative information does not imply high absolute precision. Residual persistence does not establish the tested AR(1) law. This conditional method result adds no SST observation and cannot separate arbitrary climate evolution from unknown offsets.

display.caption: Information, efficiency and fixed-record ratio sensitivity under stationary AR(1) covariances. Curves are not confidence intervals.

citations.reason: Exact signed monthly inputs and five model responses.
Independent-noise bound and its covariance limitation set this extension.
